pr_title: Automatically disable threaded NavigationMesh bake on unsupported OS
pr_body:
Automatically disables threaded NavigationMesh bake with fallback to single-thread when OS does not support multiple-threads.

Fixes #58098

issue_context.title: NavigationMesh is not being generated at all for HTML5 games
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

3.5.beta1.mono

### System information

Windows 10, GLES2

### Issue description

When generating a NavigationMesh by using the `bake_navigation_mesh` function at runtime, the navigation mesh won't be generated at all for HTML5 games. Desktop works fine tho.

When running the minimal project as desktop application it immediately prints "baking done" and you can see the navmesh when debug navigation is toggled. In browser it will never print "baking done".
Prebaked navigation meshes are visible as intended.

### Steps to reproduce

Just run the minimal reproduction project, it should show the issue clearly

### Minimal reproduction project

[MinimalProjectHTML5Navigation.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/8061861/MinimalProjectHTML5Navigation.zip)

review_comments:
With the above approach, it is possible the user will ask navigation mesh to bake on the thread but Godot will silently do it off thread. IMHO that's wrong. As a user, in the situation when I `bake(true)` and the platform does not support threading, I'd expect a warning (in case of fallback to off-thread baking) or error (in case we block such scenario entirely).

I guess lots of users used to not care about warnings, so a warning about auto fallback may be overlooked - yet it may have a severe impact on performance. Therefore I'd say we should issue an error asking one to not use `on_thread=true` in such case.

I guess a user warn_print() in the editor cannot hurt while a red error might be too much. Should still turn threaded baking off automatically in my opinion cause on_thread is true by default. A crash or not baked navmesh is worse than a framerate stutter. If framerate has problems on certain export platforms users usually begin to look at warnings and logs to notice this problem.
Ok, let's add warning - if someone will complain we will make it an error then.
